hero.lead: A nation of 11.9 million, home to the institutions of the European Union, with a €5.24 billion EU recovery and resilience plan of grants and loans.

capital.heading: The host of Europe, and a living income for every household.

register.name: OLO 108, five-year benchmark bond
register.detail: Belgian Debt Agency · syndicated 12 May 2026 · matures 22 August 2031 · coupon 3.100% · re-offer yield 3.124% · orderbook above €45bn
register.note: A new five-year benchmark; the orderbook passed €45 billion at closing
register.text: A new five-year benchmark bond of the Kingdom of Belgium, issued by syndication with an annual coupon of 3.100% and a spread of 19 basis points over mid-swaps. It is part of the OLO issuance the Belgian Debt Agency plans for 2026.

register.name: Federal government bonds (OLOs), 2026
register.detail: Belgian Debt Agency · 2025 Review – 2026 Outlook, 26 January 2026 · gross borrowing requirements €59.55bn · 2025: €45.7bn of OLOs issued
register.note: Planned OLO issuance for 2026, €5.90 billion more than in 2025, with three new benchmarks launched by syndication
register.text: The Belgian Debt Agency plans to issue €51.60 billion of OLOs in 2026, within gross borrowing requirements of €59.55 billion, and €0.40 billion of State Notes. In 2025 it issued €45.709 billion of OLOs.

register.name: OLO 106, ten-year benchmark bond
register.detail: Belgian Debt Agency · syndicated 7 January 2026 · matures 22 June 2036 · coupon 3.40% · re-offer yield 3.436% · orderbook over €91bn from over 365 investors
register.note: The first syndication of 2026, in place of the January auction; demand above €91 billion
register.text: A new ten-year benchmark bond of the Kingdom of Belgium, issued by syndication with an annual coupon of 3.40%. Demand grew to over €91 billion from more than 365 investors.

register.name: Green OLOs, 2025
register.detail: Belgian Debt Agency · green OLO 96 (April 2039) reopened for €2.1bn · green OLO 86 (April 2033) reopened in October 2025 · no new green OLO planned for 2026
register.note: Green OLOs issued in 2025 by reopening the Kingdom’s two outstanding green bonds
register.text: The Kingdom of Belgium issued €2.7 billion of green OLOs in 2025 by reopening its two outstanding green bonds, OLO 96 and OLO 86, which finance eligible green expenditure. The Belgian Debt Agency estimates green eligible expenditures at €5.0 billion; both bonds can be reopened in 2026.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · grants €5.03bn, loans €0.21bn (amended, Council document of 25 August 2026) · fifth payment request of €225M assessed positively 27 July 2026 · fifth instalment decision 21 September 2026
register.note: Loans reduced in 2026 from €230.1 million to €209.6 million; grants unchanged at €5.03 billion
register.text: EU support for Belgium’s reforms and investments under the Recovery and Resilience Facility: €5,033,950,235 in grants and €209,604,000 in loans, paid in instalments against agreed milestones and targets. The fifth payment request, submitted on 17 April 2026, covered 19 milestones and targets, among them housing renovation and unemployment benefits; all measures were due by August 2026.

register.name: Princess Elisabeth Island, phase 2 (Elia Transmission Belgium)
register.detail: EIB · project 20250041 · green credit facility signed 17 July 2026 · first drawdown around the end of July 2026 · after €650M for phase 1 in 2024 · total cost about €2,296M
register.note: The largest financing the EIB has granted to an energy infrastructure project in the Benelux
register.text: An EIB green credit facility to Elia Transmission Belgium for the electrical infrastructure of the Princess Elisabeth Island, an artificial island about 45 km off the Belgian coast that will link offshore wind farms to the onshore grid through a 220 kV substation and six 220 kV cables. The first offshore wind farms in the Princess Elisabeth Zone are to be connected from 2031; it serves the energy standard with clean power.

register.name: Affordable housing finance in Brussels (Fonds du Logement)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approval announced 19 June 2026 · socially targeted mortgages and renovations
register.note: Wider access to affordable housing finance for households in the Brussels-Capital Region
register.text: A CEB loan to the Fonds du Logement de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale to increase access to affordable housing finance for households in the capital region, with a focus on socially targeted mortgage lending and renovations. It serves the shelter standard.
by: Fonds du Logement de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale

register.name: Flanders social housing
register.detail: EIB · project 20250067 · €1.7bn agreement with the Flemish Region · first tranche of €700M signed 10 December 2025 · announced 22 January 2026 · total cost about €2,545M
register.note: About 6,350 new social housing units and the energy renovation of 10,100 more
register.text: The EIB’s largest financing in Belgium, a €1.7 billion agreement with the Flemish Region, through the Flemish social housing company VMSW, to build about 6,350 new social housing units and renovate 10,100 existing units for energy efficiency. It serves the shelter standard and lowers energy bills for tenants, mainly middle- and lower-income households.

register.name: Home energy renovation in Wallonia (SWCS)
register.detail: EIB · signed 11 December 2025 in Namur · first tranche of a €500M package to be drawn over three years · Rénopack and Rénoprêt loans
register.note: More than 16,500 energy retrofits of single-family homes and flats by the end of 2027
register.text: An EIB loan to the Société wallonne du crédit social (SWCS), the first tranche of a €500 million package, to finance energy efficiency retrofits of homes through its Rénopack and Rénoprêt loans. It is to finance more than 16,500 retrofits by the end of 2027, reaching the region’s most vulnerable households; it serves the shelter and energy standards.

register.name: Mental health infrastructure in Leuven and Kortenberg (Z.org KU Leuven)
register.detail: EIB · release of 11 December 2025 · part of a programme of about €270M for 2026–2040
register.note: The redesign of the Kortenberg psychiatric campus, a psychiatric nursing home in Lubbeek and a health and wellbeing centre in Leuven
register.text: An EIB loan to Z.org KU Leuven, the mental health network linked to KU Leuven, for the redesign of the psychiatric campus in Kortenberg, a new psychiatric nursing home in Lubbeek and a municipal health and wellbeing centre in Leuven. It serves the health standard; the EIB-financed parts are to be completed by 2036.

register.name: Sustainability investments of small businesses (Wallonie Entreprendre)
register.detail: EIB · 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Belgium, 2 February 2026
register.note: A collaboration to help small businesses with their sustainability investments
register.text: EIB financing in a €100 million collaboration with Wallonie Entreprendre to help small businesses with their sustainability investments. It serves the livelihood standard through small businesses.

register.name: Small entrepreneurs in Brussels (finance&invest.brussels)
register.detail: EIB · 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Belgium, 2 February 2026
register.note: Support for small entrepreneurs in the Brussels-Capital Region
register.text: A €50 million EIB deal with finance&invest.brussels in support of small entrepreneurs in the Brussels-Capital Region. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Flanders smart wastewater and sludge management (Aquafin)
register.detail: EIB · project 20240877 · signed 31 July 2025 · Aquafin investment programme 2025–2028 · total cost about €531M
register.note: Sewers, stormwater drainage and treatment plants for a service area of nearly seven million people
register.text: An EIB loan to Aquafin that co-finances part of its 2025–2028 investment programme in Flanders: sewage collectors, stormwater drainage, pumping stations, wastewater treatment plants and two sludge dryers that run on residual heat. It serves the water standard and sanitation, part of the shelter standard, for a service area of nearly seven million people.

register.name: ING loans for sustainable SMEs and mid-caps in Belgium
register.detail: EIB · €400M loan to ING, matched by ING · €800M in all for the Netherlands and Belgium · announced 15 April 2026
register.note: The share for companies in Belgium; €500 million goes to ING business customers in the Netherlands
register.text: An EIB loan to ING, matched by the bank, that makes €800 million available for small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps to invest in sustainability, of which €300 million for companies in Belgium. The EIB’s terms let businesses borrow at lower interest rates; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Microfinance across Belgium (microStart)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 12 November 2025 · programme loan backed by the EU through the InvestEU Fund · in progress
register.note: Microloans for people shut out of conventional banking, notably migrants, women, unemployed and young people
register.text: A CEB programme loan to microStart, a social-economy cooperative, for its on-lending across Belgium to people shut out of conventional banking who start a business or become self-employed. It serves the livelihood standard, the furthest from reach in Belgium.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Neat fields and a brick farmhouse in Flanders, Belgium

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A cobbled square of gabled guild houses in Brussels, Belgium

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Beech forest in autumn colours in the Ardennes, Belgium

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: Offshore wind turbines in the North Sea and power lines on the coast, Belgium

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: The river Meuse in a wooded valley with limestone cliffs, Belgium

items.name: microStart
items.text: A social-economy cooperative that grants microcredits, with support, to people facing financial and social inequality who want to start or grow a business, many of them excluded from bank credit. In 2025 it granted 538 microcredits worth about €4.96 million from offices in Brussels, Ghent, Antwerp, Liège and Hainaut.

items.name: DUO for a JOB
items.text: An intergenerational mentoring programme that matches young job seekers with a migrant background with volunteer mentors to help them find work. Since 2013 it has created 9,032 duos in Belgium, from offices in Antwerp, Brussels, Hainaut, Liège and East Flanders, and reports that 70% of the young people get a job, an internship or a training.

items.name: Epi St Gilles
items.text: A social grocery in Saint-Gilles, Brussels, that sells quality food, cleaning and hygiene products at reduced prices to people in precarious situations, as part of its work against poverty and for socio-professional insertion. It is one of the food aid organisations approved as a social enterprise in the Brussels-Capital Region.

items.name: Community Land Trust Brussels
items.text: A community land trust that owns the land while residents own their homes, with a limited resale price that keeps each home affordable and prevents speculation. In 2025 it reached 200 affordable homes inhabited on its land.

items.name: Ecopower
items.text: A citizen energy cooperative of 73,026 members that produces green electricity from its own installations, among them 29 wind turbines of 68 MW, and supplies 60,000 customers. Its POWER UP project with the city of Eeklo, completed in 2025, tackled energy poverty with social shares, solar panels on rented homes and budget monitoring.

items.name: BeCode
items.text: A coding school that has run inclusive bootcamps for job seekers since 2017: free, seven-month programmes in web development, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, open to people outside formal education, in Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent, Charleroi and Liège.
items.source: EU Digital Skills and Jobs Platform, 2026
